wiki.extract: The Malecón is a broad esplanade, roadway, and seawall that stretches for 8 km along the coast in Havana, Cuba, from the mouth of Havana Harbor in Old Havana, along the north side of the Centro Habana neighborhood and the Vedado neighborhood, ending at the mouth of the Almendares.

Old Havana is the city-center (downtown) and one of the 15 municipalities forming Havana, Cuba. It has the second highest population density in the city and contains the core of the original city of Havana. The positions of the original Walls of Havana are the modern boundaries of Old Havana.

Varadero, also referred to as Playa Azul, is a resort town in the province of Matanzas, Cuba, and one of the largest resort areas in the Caribbean. Varadero Beach is rated one of the world's best beaches in TripAdvisor's Traveler's Choice Awards since 2019, ranking at number 9 as of January 2024. Common activities include fishing and excursions to Matanzas, Cárdenas, and the Península de Zapata.

Viñales Valley is a karstic depression in Cuba. The valley has an area of 132 km2 (51 sq mi) and is located in the Sierra de los Órganos mountains, just north of Viñales in the Pinar del Río Province.

Trinidad is a town in the province of Sancti Spíritus, central Cuba. Together with the nearby Valle de los Ingenios, it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1988, because of its historical importance as a center of the sugar trade in the 18th and 19th centuries. Trinidad is one of the best-preserved cities in the Caribbean from the time when the sugar trade was the main industry in the region.

Whether they are called carnavales, charangas or parrandas, large public celebrations dating at least as far back as the 17th century are common throughout Cuba. However, among Cubans, the Carnaval of Santiago de Cuba enjoys a special status.

food_writeup: Cuban cuisine mixes Spanish, African and Caribbean influences: ropa vieja (shredded beef), moros y cristianos (black beans and rice) and lechón asado define the table. Tropical fruit, strong coffee and rum — in mojitos and Cuba libres — round out the island's food culture.
brief_history: A Spanish colony from 1511, Cuba won independence after the 1898 Spanish-American War and became a republic in 1902; Fidel Castro's 1959 revolution installed a communist state under a long-running US embargo. After Fidel's death in 2016 and Raúl Castro's retirement, Miguel Díaz-Canel leads an island in deep economic crisis.
current_conflicts: Cuba has no internal armed conflict, but it is under severe strain: a US maximum-pressure campaign since 2026 featuring an oil blockade and sanctions, a deep economic crisis with blackouts, and large-scale emigration.

main_events.headline: Fidel Castro falls ill; Raúl takes over
main_events.summary: The ailing 79-year-old leader temporarily cedes power to his brother Raúl in July, ending 47 years of personal rule.

main_events.headline: Cuba shines at first World Baseball Classic
main_events.summary: The national team reaches the final in San Diego.

sport.headline: Japan beats Cuba in WBC final
sport.summary: Cuba falls 10-6 to Japan in the inaugural World Baseball Classic final.

main_events.headline: Raúl consolidates power
main_events.summary: With Fidel absent, Raúl runs the government day-to-day.

main_events.headline: Hurricane Dean hits the east
main_events.summary: The August storm damages homes and crops in eastern Cuba.

sport.headline: Pan Am Games in Rio
sport.summary: Cuba finishes second in the medal table at the Rio Pan American Games.

main_events.headline: Raúl elected president
main_events.summary: The National Assembly formally elects Raúl Castro in February.

main_events.headline: Gustav and Ike devastate the island
main_events.summary: Two major hurricanes strike within weeks, causing billions of dollars in damage.

sport.headline: Beijing Olympics haul
sport.summary: Cuba wins 24 medals in Beijing, led by boxing and athletics.

main_events.headline: Obama eases restrictions
main_events.summary: Washington lifts limits on family travel and remittances.

main_events.headline: Economy contracts
main_events.summary: The global crisis and hurricane damage push the economy into reverse.

sport.headline: Cuba exits WBC early
sport.summary: Japan eliminates Cuba in the second round of the World Baseball Classic.

main_events.headline: Raúl frees political prisoners
main_events.summary: Dozens of dissidents are released in a deal brokered with the Catholic Church and Spain.

main_events.headline: Mass layoffs announced
main_events.summary: The government plans to shed 500,000 state jobs while expanding self-employment.

sport.headline: Mayagüez CAC Games
sport.summary: Cuba tops the medal table at the Central American and Caribbean Games in Puerto Rico.

main_events.headline: Party Congress backs reforms
main_events.summary: The Sixth PCC Congress approves Raúl's market-oriented 'updating' of the socialist model.

main_events.headline: Private businesses expand
main_events.summary: Licenses for small private enterprises surge.

sport.headline: Guadalajara Pan Am Games
sport.summary: Cuba finishes second at the Pan American Games in Mexico.

main_events.headline: Pope Benedict visits
main_events.summary: The pontiff's March visit draws huge crowds in Havana and Santiago.

main_events.headline: Mariel port project launches
main_events.summary: Brazil finances the deep-water port and special economic zone.

sport.headline: London Olympics
sport.summary: Cuba wins 14 medals in London, including five golds.

main_events.headline: Travel reform takes effect
main_events.summary: Cubans can travel abroad without exit permits for the first time in decades.

main_events.headline: Chávez dies; Venezuelan aid at risk
main_events.summary: The death of Cuba's main benefactor threatens subsidized oil supplies.

sport.headline: Cuba bows out of WBC
sport.summary: The Netherlands eliminates Cuba at the 2013 World Baseball Classic.

main_events.headline: US-Cuba thaw announced
main_events.summary: Obama and Raúl reveal secret talks on December 17 and move to restore diplomatic relations.

main_events.headline: Alan Gross freed
main_events.summary: The jailed American contractor's release unlocks the deal.

sport.headline: Veracruz CAC Games
sport.summary: Cuba competes at the Central American and Caribbean Games in Mexico.

main_events.headline: Embassies reopen
main_events.summary: The US and Cuban flags rise again in Havana and Washington in the summer.

main_events.headline: Tourism surges
main_events.summary: American visitors flood in as restrictions ease.

sport.headline: Toronto Pan Am Games
sport.summary: Cuba finishes fourth at the Pan American Games in Canada.

main_events.headline: Obama visits Havana
main_events.summary: The first sitting US president in 88 years lands in March.

main_events.headline: Fidel Castro dies
main_events.summary: The revolutionary leader dies on November 25 at 90, ending an era.

sport.headline: Rio Olympics: boxing dominates
sport.summary: Cuba wins 11 medals in Rio, with three boxing golds and Mijaín López's third wrestling gold.

main_events.headline: Trump rolls back opening
main_events.summary: New US restrictions target military-linked businesses.

main_events.headline: 'Havana syndrome' mystery
main_events.summary: Unexplained health incidents among US diplomats trigger an FBI probe and a staff drawdown.

sport.headline: Cuba reaches WBC second round
sport.summary: The team advances before bowing out at the 2017 World Baseball Classic.

main_events.headline: Díaz-Canel becomes president
main_events.summary: The National Assembly elects Miguel Díaz-Canel in April — the first non-Castro leader in six decades.

main_events.headline: New constitution drafted
main_events.summary: A referendum process begins to replace the 1976 charter.

sport.headline: Barranquilla CAC Games
sport.summary: Cuba competes at the Central American and Caribbean Games in Colombia.

main_events.headline: New constitution approved
main_events.summary: Voters back the charter in a February referendum, recognizing private property.

main_events.headline: Trump tightens embargo
main_events.summary: New travel bans and lawsuit provisions squeeze the economy.

sport.headline: Lima Pan Am Games
sport.summary: Cuba finishes sixth at the Pan American Games in Peru.

main_events.headline: COVID closes borders
main_events.summary: Tourism collapses; Cuba sends medical brigades abroad.

main_events.headline: Currency unification announced
main_events.summary: The government sets January 2021 for ending the dual-peso system.

sport.headline: Olympics delayed
sport.summary: Cuban athletes' Tokyo preparations are disrupted by the pandemic.

main_events.headline: July 11 protests erupt
main_events.summary: Thousands take to the streets in the largest demonstrations in decades over shortages and blackouts; hundreds are arrested.

main_events.headline: Díaz-Canel takes party helm
main_events.summary: He succeeds Raúl as Communist Party First Secretary in April.

sport.headline: Tokyo Olympics: seven golds
sport.summary: Cuba wins 15 medals in Tokyo, including Mijaín López's record fourth wrestling gold.

main_events.headline: Matanzas oil depot fire
main_events.summary: A lightning strike ignites a deadly week-long blaze in August.

main_events.headline: Hurricane Ian strikes
main_events.summary: The September storm devastates western Cuba.

main_events.headline: Family Code approved
main_events.summary: Voters back same-sex marriage in a September referendum.

sport.headline: Cuban boxers turn professional
sport.summary: State-sanctioned professionals debut as the amateur system's grip loosens.

main_events.headline: Díaz-Canel re-elected by Assembly
main_events.summary: The National Assembly grants him a second five-year term in April.

main_events.headline: Migration exodus accelerates
main_events.summary: Hundreds of thousands leave amid the deepening economic crisis.

sport.headline: Cuba reaches WBC semifinals
sport.summary: The national team falls to the USA in Miami in its best Classic showing in years.

main_events.headline: Blackouts plunge island into darkness
main_events.summary: Nationwide grid failures in October leave millions without power for days.

main_events.headline: Hurricanes Oscar and Rafael hit
main_events.summary: Two late-season storms compound the energy crisis.

sport.headline: Mijaín López wins fifth straight gold
sport.summary: The wrestler's Paris triumph makes Olympic history: five consecutive individual golds in the same event.

main_events.headline: Trump's return deepens pressure
main_events.summary: Washington signals a renewed maximum-pressure campaign as Cuba's crisis worsens.

main_events.headline: Emigration hollows out towns
main_events.summary: Population decline accelerates amid shortages of food, fuel and medicine.

sport.headline: Baseball talent drain continues
sport.summary: Top players keep defecting as the domestic league withers.
